key_insight: RIS can reproduce the main hemodynamic behavior of aortic valve FSI simulations at much lower cost, making it a practical surrogate when realistic leaflet kinematics are available.
engineering_relevance: For valve design and patient-specific studies, RIS offers a computationally efficient way to estimate transvalvular pressure and flow patterns without fully coupled structural solves.
method: Compared prescribed-kinematics RIS in SimVascular svMultiPhysics with fully coupled IB in IBAMR.
Tested trileaflet and bicuspid aortic valve configurations.
Assessed bulk flow structures and transvalvular pressure gradients, plus computational cost.
evidence_signal: RIS matched large-scale flow features and predicted mean transvalvular pressure gradient within 15% of IB, improving to within 5% when inlet conditions were matched, while cutting cost by about 60%.
watch_item: RIS depends on prescribed leaflet motion, so accuracy can degrade if the kinematics are not representative of the true valve dynamics.
paper_title: Comparative analysis of resistive immersed surface and immersed boundary methods for aortic valve simulation
